The Production Over Expected (POE) Framework

Raw college production is not comparable across situations. Eighty receptions in the SEC is not eighty receptions in the MAC, and 1,200 yards behind a top offensive line is not 1,200 yards behind a bottom-tier one.

POE adjusts raw college production for contextual factors — conference strength, offensive line quality, QB talent, surrounding competition — to isolate what the prospect actually did vs. what anyone in their position would have done.

It carries the highest weight in the WR model — over 50% of the total. That is a statement about how the model was fit, not about how often it is right: the out-of-sample validation noted above is still outstanding.

What POE Adjusts For

Conference Strength
SEC production weighted differently than Group of 5
O-Line Quality
RB rushing yards adjusted for blocking grades
QB Talent
WR production adjusted for passer quality
Surrounding Competition
Target share context — was he WR1 by default?

RB Archetype Framework

After the model initially undervalued speed backs like De'Von Achane, the RB evaluation was rebuilt with archetype-specific criteria:

Zone Backs
Vision, patience, one-cut ability. Key metric: yards after contact per attempt
Power Backs
Contact balance, short-yardage conversion. Key metric: broken tackle rate
Receiving Backs
Route-running, catch radius. Key metric: yards per route run
Speed Backs
Breakaway rate, acceleration. Key metric: speed build ratio

The GENERATIONAL Label

GENERATIONAL is reserved only for prospects who truly break the model — players whose POE is so far above the regression line that the model can't explain them with contextual factors alone. In the 2018-2023 training data, only a handful of prospects earned this designation.

Read the full article on GENERATIONAL vs. Elite →

Model Validation
The model has been run back over the 2023 class and read against what those players went on to do. That is a retrospective check on one class, not validation: the outcomes were already known when the thresholds were set. A real test — scoring classes the model has never seen and grading it on three-year outcomes — has not been run yet, and this panel will carry its results when it has.
2023 WRs 6 of the top 7 producers
2023 RBs top 3 correct
Notable miss Puka Nacua
Known bias Small-school power backs
Key Input Metrics
WR: POE (50%+ weight), YPRR, contested catch %, dominator rating, breakout age
RB: Archetype classification, breakaway rate, speed build ratio, contact balance metrics
Both: Binary breakout age threshold (19.5 years), medical/workload discount factors
NFL Success: Top-12 positional scrimmage yards within 3 seasons

"GENERATIONAL should only be saved for ones who truly break the model."
